title: Microsoft Updates Copilot App, Merges Personal Chats and Retires Key AI Features
content_md: Microsoft is consolidating its consumer and productivity-focused AI experiences through a major update to the Copilot app, combining chat histories and content for personal users while retiring several high-profile features, including Podcasts , Deep Research, and Group Chat. The changes arrive alongside Microsoft’s broader branding shift from the Microsoft 365 (Office) app to the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, which began rolling out on January 15, 2025. The renamed application is now used across Windows, iOS, Android, and the web, with office.com and microsoft365.com redirecting users to the m365.cloud.microsoft domain. Microsoft Updates Copilot App, Merges Personal Chats Microsoft says the updated Copilot app is intended to provide a more cohesive experience across work, school, and personal contexts. Users can sign in with a personal Microsoft account, a work or school account, or both, using an account switcher to separate experiences. For users who access both the standalone Microsoft Copilot app and the Microsoft 365 Copilot app with a personal account, chat histories and Copilot-created content will be merged into a single updated application. Microsoft said chats, images, and other user-created material will migrate during the transition. Despite the consolidation, Microsoft stressed that the boundaries between personal and enterprise data remain intact.
